value.body: A two-year master's degree in engineering (M.Tech, or M.E. at some universities). You specialise more deeply in one area — for example Computer Science, VLSI, Structural, Thermal, Power Systems, Data Science or Machine Design — and the second year is largely a research project and thesis. It leads to R&D and design roles, teaching, and a PhD.

items.label: Course length
items.note: 4 semesters; part-time and sponsored options exist at some institutes

items.label: GATE test-takers
items.note: Summed across papers (two-paper candidates counted twice); about 1 in 5 qualified
items.source: GATE 2025 Statistical and Performance Report (IIT Roorkee)

items.label: AICTE PG scholarship
items.note: For GATE-qualified students admitted to eligible AICTE-approved institutes, up to 24 months

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.Tech / B.E. (or a relevant M.Sc / MCA for some programmes) and, for most seats, a valid GATE score. IITs offer seats through COAP (Common Offer Acceptance Portal); NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded institutes admit through CCMT counselling. Many state and private universities use GATE, a state PG test (such as TS PGECET, AP PGECET or TANCET) or their own entrance test.

value.title: At a glance
items: A GATE score is valid for three years, so it can be used for M.Tech admission a year or two after graduating.
The same GATE score is used by several PSUs for recruitment, so some candidates weigh an M.Tech against a PSU job.
M.Tech is a common step towards a PhD or an engineering-college teaching post.
GATE score cut-offs differ widely by institute, specialisation and category, and shift every year.
